_meta.what: Follow-the-money dossier for Ahmedabad land — how political/bureaucratic/corporate/foreign elites capture the value uplift on the city's land, especially the western periphery. Each entry: {actor, role, how_they_profit, mechanism, project, tier, claim, source, denial_if_any}.

tier_legend.A: DOCUMENTED FACT — TP-scheme records, land auctions, project structure, official figures, statute, court/ED records. Stated as fact, with source.
tier_legend.B: REPORTED ALLEGATION — black money, benami, favouritism, drug-money/laundering. Framed as 'alleged/reported by [named source]', NEVER asserted as fact; denials included where on record.
tier_legend.C: ANALYSIS — the mechanism / our reading. Not a factual claim about any named person's conduct.

_meta.hard_rule: This is a PUBLIC repository naming powerful people and firms. No unproven criminality is asserted as fact. Tier-B items are clearly-attributed reported allegations only. The documentable CORE is the lawful land-value-capture mechanism (Tier A + C), not any crime.
_meta.frame: Ghosh (the municipality/improvement-trust as a 'recoupment' rent machine — selling surplus acquired-and-improved land at a value 'rendered from the future') + Cooper (privatization of public goods and asset-price inflation as counterrevolution against democratic claims on the economy). AUDA is the improvement trust reborn; the TP scheme is recoupment, industrialised.
_meta.mega_event_clarification: The Commonwealth Games were DELHI 2010, not Ahmedabad. Ahmedabad's actual mega-event pipeline: the 2036 Summer Olympics BID (Ahmedabad as India's lead candidate city; India entered the IOC 'Continuous Dialogue' phase Aug 2025), the 2029-era National Games / multi-sport build-out, and G20 (2023) venue use. The land mechanism is the same regardless of which event lands.
_meta.status: Authored 2026-06 from public institutional fact, statute, official figures and named reporting. Allegation entries cite the named source and the subject's stated position.

entries.role: Statutory urban development authority — the land-assembly machine for the peri-urban area outside AMC limits
entries.how_they_profit: Captures the value uplift on peri-urban land. Under the Town Planning Scheme (TPS) it pools all land parcels in an area, deducts up to ~40% of each owner's land for roads/parks/amenities AND for a saleable reserve, returns ~60% as serviced 'final plots' worth far more, and then AUCTIONS the land it retained at the new, uplifted, infrastructure-bearing value. Plus a betterment charge (one-half of the value increase) on the returned plots.
entries.mechanism: Land pooling + reconstitution ('readjustment') under the Gujarat Town Planning & Urban Development Act, 1976. Ahmedabad is the first Indian city to implement ~90% of its Development Plan through TPS; sale of TPS-acquired land is a major AUDA revenue source. This is Ghosh's colonial-trust 'recoupment' running a century on: the body acquires, improves, and sells the surplus at a future-rendered value.
entries.project: AUDA TP Schemes across the western periphery (Bopal, South Bopal, Shela, Shilaj, SG Highway corridor, Sanand side); the 76-km Sardar Patel (SP) Ring Road assembled via TPS land
entries.claim: AUDA assembles, reconstitutes and releases peri-urban land under the GTPUDA 1976, capturing the value uplift through retained-plot sales and betterment charges; ~90% of Ahmedabad's Development Plan is delivered via TPS and TPS land sales are a core AUDA income stream.
entries.source: Gujarat Town Planning & Urban Development Act, 1976 (data/laws/ahmedabad/gtpuda-1976.pdf); World Resources Institute, 'Ahmedabad: Town Planning Schemes for Equitable Development — Glass Half Full or Half Empty?'; Lincoln Institute / Ballaney & Patel, 'Town Planning Schemes as a Hybrid Land Readjustment Process in Ahmedabad'; GI Hub 'Ahmedabad Land Pooling Scheme' case study.

entries.actor: Periphery landowners (large agricultural landholders on the western fringe)
entries.role: Original owners of fringe agricultural land brought into a TP scheme
entries.how_they_profit: Surrender up to ~40% of land but keep ~60% reconstituted as serviced urban plots whose value multiplies once roads, the Ring Road and trunk services arrive. The uplift on the retained 60% typically dwarfs the value of the surrendered 40% plus betterment charge.
entries.mechanism: TPS reconstitution: only REGISTERED landowners participate in scheme design; renters, informal settlers and the landless get nothing. The gain accrues to whoever holds title when the area is notified — which rewards early/speculative acquisition of fringe farmland.
entries.project: Bopal / South Bopal / Shela / Shilaj / Sanand-side TP schemes along the SP Ring Road and SG Highway
entries.claim: TPS distributes the value uplift to registered landowners (who keep ~60% as serviced plots) while excluding non-owners from both the process and the gain; valuation is done in a 'roundabout' way with large gaps between assessed and market values.
entries.source: World Resources Institute TPS study (equity critique: only registered owners participate; renters/informal settlers marginalized); Lincoln Institute / MIT (Ballaney) land-readjustment papers; coecept/Human Habitats analysis.

entries.actor: Western-periphery real-estate developers and land aggregators (SG Highway / Bopal / Shela / Sanand-GIFT corridor)
entries.role: Buyers, aggregators and builders on the reconstituted, Ring-Road-served fringe
entries.how_they_profit: Buy or aggregate fringe land ahead of (or at) TPS notification and Ring-Road / SG Highway servicing, then sell built product into a rising market. Documented price escalation: SP Ring Road West apartments ~Rs 5,950/sq ft (2026), up ~+42.9% over five years; Shela/South Bopal/Shilaj ~Rs 4,500-6,000/sq ft; SG Highway/Thaltej/Satellite Rs 6,000+/sq ft.
entries.mechanism: Value capture by anticipation: the state announces an infrastructure line (SP Ring Road, opened 2004 at ~Rs 355 cr; metro; SG Highway widening), land in its catchment re-prices, and whoever holds title captures the jump. This is Cooper's asset-price inflation as the real engine of accumulation.
entries.project: SP Ring Road corridor; SG Highway; Bopal–South Bopal–Shela–Shilaj; the Sanand-toward-GIFT axis
entries.claim: Western-periphery land and housing prices escalated sharply along the SP Ring Road / SG Highway corridor (e.g. SP Ring Road West +~43% over five years to ~Rs 5,950/sq ft in 2026), capturing the publicly-funded infrastructure uplift.
entries.source: Sardar Patel Ring Road (Wikipedia: 76 km, ~Rs 355 cr, opened 2004, built by AUDA); 99acres SP Ring Road West / Ahmedabad property-rate trends (May-2026); AddressOfChoice SP Ring Road guide.

entries.actor: SRFDCL (Sabarmati Riverfront Development Corporation Ltd) — an AMC SPV
entries.role: Special-purpose vehicle that reclaimed and commercialised land from the Sabarmati riverbed
entries.how_they_profit: Self-finances by selling/leasing the land it MANUFACTURED. ~202.79 ha reclaimed from the river; ~14% earmarked for commercial/residential sale; in 2020 SRFDCL appointed JLL India to monetise ~500 acres (~200 ha) valued at ~Rs 3,500 crore. The project's capital model is: create new land from a public river, sell the prime fraction to fund the whole.
entries.mechanism: Land manufacture + recoupment: an SPV (off the elected AMC's direct books) narrows the river to reclaim hundreds of hectares of brand-new, central, high-value land, then sells the commercial slice. Textbook Ghosh recoupment — 'rehousing the poor became an idle afterthought.'
entries.claim: SRFDCL reclaimed ~202.79 ha from the Sabarmati and commercialised a portion (~14% commercial/residential); in 2020 it engaged JLL to monetise ~500 acres valued at ~Rs 3,500 crore.
entries.source: Sabarmati Riverfront (Wikipedia: 202.79 ha reclaimed; JLL 2020 mandate, ~500 acres, ~Rs 3,500 cr); SRFDCL master plan; Urban Design Lab project profile.

entries.role: Prior occupants of the riverbank — the cost-bearers of the riverfront's land value
entries.how_they_profit: They do not. They are the debit side of the recoupment ledger. A 2003 survey counted 14,555 slum households along the bank, of which ~6,293 were assessed as needing rehabilitation; reporting describes >10,000 residents displaced and inadequate, deteriorating resettlement (e.g. Santosh Nagar).
entries.mechanism: Value transfer: central riverbank land is converted from informal-settlement use to saleable commercial frontage; the uplift accrues to the SPV and its buyers, the displacement cost falls on evicted households. (Tier A on the displacement figures and rehab shortfall as documented/reported; the value-transfer reading is Tier C.)
entries.claim: The riverfront displaced over 10,000 riverbank residents (2003 survey: 14,555 slum households, ~6,293 needing rehabilitation); rehabilitation has been widely reported as inadequate and the resettlement housing as deteriorating.
entries.source: Down To Earth, 'Concerns over Sabarmati Riverfront Development Project'; Land Conflict Watch, 'Slum Dwellers in Gujarat Displaced by Sabarmati Riverfront Await Rehabilitation'; NLS Student Law Review; 1997 EPC study & 2003 survey figures cited therein.

entries.actor: Government of Gujarat / GIFTCL / GUDCL (Gujarat Urban Development Company)
entries.role: Owner-developer of GIFT City after buying out IL&FS
entries.how_they_profit: Holds and monetises the GIFT City land bank and SEZ. Originally a 50:50 JV with IL&FS; when IL&FS collapsed, GUDCL (for the Gujarat government) bought out the 50% stake for ~Rs 32 crore equity value (concluded June 2020), giving the state full ownership of GIFTCL and its 100%-subsidiary GIFT SEZ Ltd. The state then allots/leases built-up area to financial firms and developers.
entries.mechanism: State-as-landlord of a financial-SEZ enclave: an SPV outside the elected AMC/AUDA, on the Gandhinagar side, assembles land and captures the rent of India's flagship IFSC. Cooper's frame: a tax-privileged offshore-onshore financial zone built by the state as a public good but operated to attract and house private capital.
entries.project: GIFT City (Gujarat International Finance Tec-City) / GIFT IFSC / GIFT SEZ
entries.claim: GIFT City is a Gujarat-government-owned SPV (GIFTCL via GUDCL) after the state bought out IL&FS's 50% stake for ~Rs 32 cr equity (June 2020); GIFT SEZ Ltd is its 100% subsidiary and SEZ developer.
entries.source: GIFT City (Wikipedia); The Tribune, 'IL&FS sells 50% stake in GIFT City to Gujarat government'; The Wire (Nov 2018); GIFT SEZ Ltd structure.

entries.actor: GIFT City private developers / occupiers (e.g. Hiranandani, Brigade, Savvy, Shivalik, and IFSC financial institutions)
entries.role: Allottees of built-up area and office space inside GIFT SEZ / IFSC
entries.how_they_profit: Receive allotments of built-up area on state-assembled land in a tax-privileged zone. Brigade Enterprises was allotted ~1.1 million sq ft (Oct 2014); Hiranandani ~0.25 million sq ft (its 'Signature' tower is India's first fully functional commercial tower in the IFSC); residential parcels went to Savvy, Shivalik, Brigade and others; 20+ financial institutions took IFSC office space. ~50% of GIFT's built-up area was allotted by late 2025, with full allotment projected by ~2030.
entries.mechanism: Private capture of a state-built financial enclave's land and tax advantages — the public assembles and services the land; private allottees and IFSC firms enjoy the location rent and the SEZ/IFSC tax regime.
entries.claim: Private developers (Brigade ~1.1M sq ft 2014; Hiranandani ~0.25M sq ft; Savvy, Shivalik et al.) and 20+ IFSC financial institutions are allotted built-up area on the state-assembled GIFT land; ~50% allotted by late 2025.
entries.source: GujaratProperty / DeshGujarat ('Half of GIFT City's built-up area allotted', 28-Nov-2025); Hiranandani Communities 'Signature' GIFT City; Brigade Enterprises allotment (9-Oct-2014); giftgujarat.in occupancy details.

entries.actor: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Sports Enclave / Ahmedabad 2036 Olympic-bid land assembly (state sports-infra programme)
entries.role: Mega-event land machine — the justification for large-scale public land assembly in the northwest
entries.how_they_profit: A mega-event re-zones and re-prices the periphery. The enclave covers ~355 acres in Motera by the Narendra Modi Stadium; a second hub (Karai Sports Hub, ~143 acres) is 'augmented by reclaimed riverfront'; a further enclave is planned at Naranpura. Ahmedabad is India's lead 2036 Olympic candidate (IOC 'Continuous Dialogue' from Aug 2025); construction from 2026. The event narrative justifies acquisition and spikes surrounding land values.
entries.mechanism: Mega-event-as-value-trigger: Olympic/National-Games branding legitimises assembling hundreds of acres and pours public infrastructure into the northwest (Motera/Sabarmati), lifting periphery land values — Cooper's 'extravagance' (spectacle spending) fused with Ghosh's recoupment (publicly-funded uplift captured around the venue).
entries.project: SVP Sports Enclave (Motera, ~355 acres) + Karai Sports Hub (~143 acres) + Naranpura enclave; Ahmedabad 2036 Olympic bid; National Games / G20 (2023) venue pipeline
entries.claim: Ahmedabad is India's lead 2036 Olympic candidate city (IOC 'Continuous Dialogue' from Aug 2025); the SVP Sports Enclave (~355 acres, Motera) and Karai Sports Hub (~143 acres, partly on reclaimed riverfront) are being assembled, with construction from 2026 — the mega-event justifying large public land assembly in the northwest. (NB: the Commonwealth Games were Delhi 2010, not Ahmedabad.)
entries.source: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Sports Enclave (Wikipedia); Populous 'Ahmedabad Olympic Park Masterplan'; Swarajya, 'India's 2036 Olympics Bid: Ahmedabad At The Centre'; t2online coverage.

entries.actor: Torrent Power (Mehta family) and Adani Group (airport)
entries.role: Private monopoly operators of Ahmedabad's privatised civic infrastructure (context for who already holds the city's chokepoints)
entries.how_they_profit: Torrent holds the city's entire electricity distribution (private licensee since 1915; control consolidated 1997/2006); Adani holds Ahmedabad's SVPI airport on a 50-year AAI concession (from 2020). Both earn regulated/concession returns on essential urban infrastructure citizens cannot vote out.
entries.mechanism: Privatised provisioning: high-value infrastructure carved out of the elected corporation and run as a private monopoly answerable to a regulator (GERC/AERA), not the ballot. (Land-rent relevance: airport-zone and power-served land both feed periphery value.)
entries.project: Torrent Power Ahmedabad licence area; Adani SVPI airport concession
entries.claim: Ahmedabad's electricity distribution is a Torrent (Mehta-family) private monopoly; its airport is on a 50-year Adani concession from 2020 — both essential services outside the elected corporation.
entries.source: data/institutions/privatization_map.json (sourced to Torrent Power 'About Us'; AAI concession 14-Feb-2020; Adani SVPIA).

entries.actor: Real-estate 'cash component' / benami holders on the periphery (UNNAMED — pattern, not a named person)
entries.role: Subject of reported black-money/benami allegations in Gujarat land deals
entries.how_they_profit: ALLEGED: holding property via benami (no-name) arrangements and transacting a large unaccounted cash component to launder/park black money in periphery land — a pattern repeatedly reported in Indian real estate generally and named in some Gujarat-linked ED actions.
entries.mechanism: Periphery land as a black-money sink: rapidly appreciating, opaquely-valued fringe land is a classic vehicle for parking unaccounted cash and benami holdings. (Tier C as a mechanism; any specific person's conduct would be Tier B and must be individually sourced.)
entries.project: Western-periphery land market generally; specific ED actions where named
entries.claim: REPORTED/ALLEGED: benami holdings and unaccounted cash components are used to park black money in Gujarat/periphery land. This is reported as a pattern; it is NOT asserted as fact against any named individual here. Example of an ED action touching Ahmedabad-area land: the ED has attached land parcels in Sanand (Ahmedabad) in proceedings against the Reliance Anil Ambani (ADAG) group — reported by Business Standard and others; ADAG entities have generally contested ED proceedings and asserted compliance.
entries.source: Directorate of Enforcement (enforcementdirectorate.gov.in); Business Standard reporting on ED benami/land attachments incl. Sanand parcels in ADAG proceedings. (No unsourced naming.)
entries.denial_if_any: Subjects of ED proceedings generally deny wrongdoing and contest attachments; ADAG group entities have publicly asserted full compliance and challenged ED actions. Specific denials must be cited per named case.

entries.actor: Adani Ports & SEZ (APSEZ) — Mundra Port (the 'drugs' angle, strictly as reported)
entries.role: Operator of Mundra Port, Gujarat — site of a major narcotics seizure repeatedly raised in 'drug-money/laundering' commentary
entries.how_they_profit: N/A to any crime — APSEZ profits lawfully as India's largest port operator. This entry exists ONLY to handle the user's 'drugs/mafia' angle responsibly and strictly as reported, NOT to assert any link.
entries.mechanism: Included as a clearly-attributed reported event, with the operator's stated position. No link to Ahmedabad land laundering is asserted; none is sourced.
entries.project: Mundra Port (Kutch, Gujarat) — not Ahmedabad land, included for the user's stated 'drugs' query
entries.claim: REPORTED/DOCUMENTED EVENT: On 16 Sept 2021 the DRI (Ministry of Finance) seized ~2,988.21 kg of heroin (originating Afghanistan, shipped via Bandar Abbas, Iran) from two containers at Adani-operated Mundra Port — described as among the largest heroin seizures in India. Some commentators (e.g. former MP Jawhar Sircar; Adani Watch) publicly questioned why Mundra was used and called for government takeover. NO finding has tied Adani Ports to the contraband, and NO link between this seizure and Ahmedabad land/real-estate laundering is asserted or sourced here.
entries.source: Business Today, 19-Nov-2021 ('customs, DRI team seized hazardous cargo containers at Mundra Port'); Al Jazeera, 12-Oct-2021; Business Standard, 21-Sept-2021 ('We've no policing authority over containers: Adani Group'); The Tribune (Finance Ministry quizzed APSEZ); Adani Watch.
entries.denial_if_any: Adani Group stated it is a port operator with NO policing authority over containers: under the Customs Act only government authorities (Customs/DRI) may open, examine and seize cargo, and 'no port operator across the country can examine a container' — their role is limited to running the port. Following the seizure, Adani Ports announced it would stop handling containerised cargo originating from Afghanistan, Iran and Pakistan (from Nov 2021). Adani Ports has not been charged in connection with the consignment.
